title: Tahini and honey cake
subtitle: Middle Eastern inspired sesame cake with honey glaze
excerpt: A tahini and honey cake has the earthiness of sesame in the sponge and a warm, floral honey glaze poured over while still warm. The tahini keeps the crumb moist and gives a slight bitterness that stops it being too sweet. The sesame flavour is present but subtle, this reads as a richly flavoured cake rather than a novelty ingredient one.
sourceNotes: Tahini-based baked goods are rooted in the Eastern Mediterranean, Levantine, and North African baking traditions. Tahini (sesame paste) is used in sweet preparations across these regions, in halva, in sesame biscuits, and in cake batters where it adds moisture and richness. The trend of using tahini in Western-style layer cakes and loaf cakes was accelerated by cookbooks by Yotam Ottolenghi and Sami Tamimi from around 2012 onward, followed by Reem Kassis and Salma Hage, all of whom bridged Levantine baking techniques with English baking contexts. The honey glaze here echoes the honey-soaked pastry tradition of baklava.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfrosted and well wrapped for up to 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 3 days; flavour improves on day 2.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 180°C or fan 160°C; skewer in the centre should come out clean

content.text: Tahini and honey cake has an earthy, slightly bitter sesame character balanced by a warm honey glaze. The tahini does two things: it replaces a portion of the butter and acts as a fat source that keeps the crumb moist for days. Use a runny, good-quality tahini, thick or separated tahini makes the batter too heavy.

Preheat the oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Grease and line a 20 cm round cake tin with parchment. Beat the butter, tahini, honey, and caster sugar together until combined and smooth, the mixture won't become as pale as an all-butter creaming because tahini is denser. Add the eggs one at a time and beat well. Fold in the flour and baking powder alternately with the milk in two additions. Pour into the tin, scatter the sesame seeds over the top, and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, warm 3 tablespoons of honey with 1 tablespoon of water in a small pan until it becomes fluid. Pour over the hot cake and leave to soak in as the cake cools. The honey glaze sets to a light, sticky sheen. Cool completely in the tin before removing.
